name: Kurai Steppe
full: An intermontane basin in the middle reaches of the Chuya between the Kurai (north) and North Chuya (south) ranges, along the Chuysky Trakt at roughly km 813–844; the main villages are Kurai and Kyzyl-Tash. The classic panorama is the North Chuya Range viewing platform at km 822.
near: Kurai village (≈427 residents, 2016; 50°13′ N, 87°55′ E; ~66 km to Kosh-Agach), Kyzyl-Tash village; Aktash village is ~30–35 km to the northwest (estimate)
elev: 1500–1600 m (basin floor; tonkosti, “Znanie”, amic.ru); vpoxod — ~1600 m
short: A high-mountain steppe ~20 km across with a frontal panorama of the North Chuya Range glaciers (Maashey-Bash 4173 m, Aktru 4044 m) and giant current ripples — traces of catastrophic glacial lake outburst floods 15,000 years ago.
desc: The Kurai Steppe is an intermontane basin in the middle reaches of the Chuya at an elevation of 1500–1600 m, about 20 km across, surrounded by mountains on all sides. To the south the glaciers of the North Chuya Range stand over it like a wall: Kurkurek, Kyzyl-Tash, Aktru (4044 m), and the highest point, Maashey-Bash (4173 m), with the largest glacier, Maashey (~10 km). The basin is famous for one of the most spectacular fields of giant current ripples in the world: ridges up to 20 m high (“frozen waves”, visible from space) were formed about 15,000 years ago, when the ice-dammed lakes of the Kurai and Chuya basins burst, with discharges of 1 to 18 million m³/s (amic.ru, vpoxod). The climate is sharply continental: the frost-free period is 55–60 days, precipitation is 150–200 mm a year, and in summer heat can suddenly give way to a snowstorm. The vegetation resembles the Mongolian desert steppes; along the Chuya there are poplar, willow, sea buckthorn and shrubby cinquefoil (Kuril tea). The steppe is rich in archaeology: ancient Turkic burial mounds, the Kezer stone statue (8th–9th centuries), rock drawings and ancient irrigation systems (the “Kurai culture”); since 2014 part of the monuments have been protected by the Mezhelik historical and cultural reserve (vpoxod). Drop-off trips to Aktru and to Lake Dzhangyskol start from Kurai; there are viewpoints nearby and lodging in ails and glamping sites.
guide: Stop at the viewing platform at km 822 — from here you can see almost the whole wall of the North Chuya Range; find the highest snow dome: that is Maashey-Bash (4173 m). Take a good look at the steppe: those even rows of hills are not dunes but ripples left by the flood from a glacial lake 15,000 years ago, as tall as a six-storey building. The artist Yegor Meyer wrote in the 19th century that he had never seen a more grandiose picture. The mountains are clearest in the morning — by lunchtime clouds gather over the glaciers. Take a warm jacket even in July: here you can get all four seasons in one day.
see: The panorama of the North Chuya Range from the viewing platform at km 822 (Kurkurek, Kyzyl-Tash, Aktru, Maashey-Bash); giant current ripples on the basin floor; the Kezer stone statue and burial mounds (Mezhelik reserve); the bridge over the Chuya; a view of the mouth of the Aktru valley.
skip: the weather is overcast and the range is hidden by clouds — without the mountains the steppe looks flat and dusty. But if you're driving the trakt to Kosh-Agach/Mars, a 10–15 minute stop at km 822 costs you almost nothing.
diff: Very easy: the viewing platform is right by the highway; walks across the steppe involve no climbing; dirt roads toward the mountains are for 4×4 / SUV only (dmitriytravel: attempts to reach Aktru end at water obstacles).
when: June–September — snow on the mountains, dry roads; September — clear air and yellow larches; winter is very cold (the basin is one of the cold poles of Altai), but the panorama is accessible from the trakt.
hours: Open terrain, open 24 hours and free.
daytime: Morning — before clouds form over the range; sunset gives a pink light on the glaciers (editorial).
how: Along the Chuysky Trakt: from Aktash to the southeast, the basin is at km 813–844 (tonkosti), the viewing platform is at km 822, Kurai village is near km 826 (the turn to Aktru — tonkosti “Aktru Glacier”). From Gorno-Altaysk ~380–390 km (estimate from the km markers), 6.5–8 h.
needcar: Yes — a car, the Gorno-Altaysk — Kosh-Agach marshrutka (minibus), or a tour; inside the steppe — a 4×4 / SUV.
self: Yes — the viewing platform is by the highway; for steppe dirt roads you need a 4×4 / SUV and a navigator.
roadtype: Paved road (R-256); in the steppe — dirt and rocky tracks with fords, a wooden bridge over the Chuya (dmitriytravel).
traveltime: Aktash → viewing platform ~30–40 min; Gorno-Altaysk → 6.5–8 h (roadworks at km 455–495 in 2026).
stay: Kurai/Kyzyl-Tash: “Vyshe Gor” (Above the Mountains) glamping (km 823, 1700 m) from 5,000 ₽ (RUB), season 01.06–01.09 (9.8/10); “Glamping Kurai” (3 km from the village, 11.06–05.09, up to 26 guests); Basecamp Aktru (mirrored houses) from 12,500 ₽ (RUB); the “Mir Altaya” (World of Altai) eco-hotel (domes, 12 km from Kurai); the “Krug Golikova” campsite; the “Stepnoy Kochevnik” (Steppe Nomad) tourist base (35 beds), the “Otdykh Kuraya” guesthouse from ~1,000 ₽ (RUB) (turistka.ru), “Altai Etno Resort” (yurts). The phone numbers on aggregators are the aggregators' booking lines.
net: not found (according to reviews, there is a signal in Kurai and patchy coverage in the steppe; not confirmed for specific operators)
entry: Free (open steppe). If you drive into the Mezhelik reserve, no fees were found.
transfer: Guided tour 57,900 ₽ (RUB)/5 days (Tripster 2026); marshrutka (minibus) to Kosh-Agach ≈4772 ₽ (RUB); a UAZ across the steppe — negotiable (Mir Altaya: from 11,000 ₽ (RUB) to Aktru).
bring: Warm, windproof clothing (sharp temperature swings), sun protection, water, binoculars/a telephoto lens for the glaciers, cash.
warn: Sudden weather changes (snow in summer), strong sun at 1500–1600 m; dirt roads toward the mountains with fords are dangerous during floods. Border zone: the border zone in Kosh-Agach district covers only part of the territory: under FSB order No. 282 (2006) — the Dzhazator, Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Kazakh, Tashanta and Kokorya settlements; by FSB order No. 512 of 13.10.2022, Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Zhana-Aul and Kokorya were additionally removed from the zone (Tashanta, Belyashi and Argut remain in the zone). Kurai, Kyzyl-Tash, Chagan-Uzun and Aktash/Chibit (Ulagan district) are not on these lists — according to the data found, no permit is needed for this place (medium confidence: no official response from the border directorate for this specific point was found). General rules: for Russian citizens a passport is enough in the border zone, and a permit is needed only for the 5-km strip along the border; foreigners need a permit for any point in the border zone (processing up to 60 days according to the Sailyugem National Park website; 15/30 days according to other sources). Where to apply: FSB Border Directorate for the Altai Republic, Gorno-Altaysk, Kommunistichesky Ave. 94, +7 388-22 4-82-00, pugornyjaltaj@mail.ru; the office in Kosh-Agach, Armeyskaya St. 2, +7 388-42 2-34-70. Keep your passport with you — document checks on the trakt are possible. Ticks: as of 25.08.2026 in the Altai Republic there were 3,600 tick-bite reports and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Rospotrebnadzor) — get vaccinated/insured.
food: The restaurant-bar of the “Vyshe Gor” glamping — regional cuisine from farm produce (mirturbaz); the cafe at “Glamping Kurai” with a summer terrace; specific dishes/prices not found.
reviews: No separate ratings found; the Tripster tour that includes the steppe — 4.54 (25 ratings). Reviews say: “a grandiose panorama”; cons — dust, wind, clouds hiding the mountains.

p.sum: A panorama by the highway: the viewing platform at km 822 (50.2508, 87.8697) — 10–30 min; Kurai (km ~826) is the base for Aktru and Dzhangyskol, with glamping sites and ails. Free, year-round; morning has the best visibility.
